title: Exchange Club of Rome salutes local law enforcement - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Carey ,
10 hours ago The Exchange Club of Rome honors Rome and Floyd County law enforcement officers and their families at their Law Enforcement Appreciation program. By Steven Eckhoff The Exchange Club of Rome recognized several local officers as part of a salute to all the law enforcement agencies in Rome and Floyd County.
The club hosted representatives of the Georgia State Patrol, Floyd County Sheriff’s Office, Rome Police Department and Floyd County Police Department at a March 20 ceremony.
“This year we gave plaques to one member of each of these agencies,” Club President Joyce Gaston said. “And we value the families who give those officers the daily support to serve our community. Each spouse was given either a beautiful bouquet of flowers or a gift card as a thanks for their service and support.”
The first person honored was Trooper First Class James S. Mitchell III from GSP Post 38.
Mitchell began his career in 1993 with the Summerville Police Department and joined the GSP in 2008 with the 86th GSP Trooper School.
“Jamie has been a strong advocate for child passenger safety, and in 2012, he presented a study to the Prosecuting Attorney’s Council of Georgia,” GSP Sgt. Doug Shamblin said. “That led to the development of a program for offenders placed on probation to donate a car seat as a term of the probation fees.”
Mitchell was also the 2026 nominee for their Trooper of the Year with Post 38, according to Shamblin.
FCSO’s public information officer, Deputy Corey Bowers, was recognized next for his 15 years in public safety.
Bowers was recently given a new assignment, taking over as the handler of K9 Officer Doc, who was previously assigned to Mike Williams, who died recently after a long illness.
Bowers has also been the public information officer, dealing with media relations and community events, a position he will continue in addition to his duties as a K9 officer.
Next, Rome Police Officer Josh Taylor was honored with the Life Safety Award for helping a woman having a mental breakdown who threatened to run into traffic on Shorter Avenue.
Taylor chased the woman down and prevented her from running in front of a car before getting her into an ambulance so she could receive treatment.
Lastly, Rome Floyd Metro Task Force Commander Sgt. Cathy Taylor was honored by FCPD Maj. Carl Lively.
Taylor has 15 years of service and joined the task force in 2019, according to Lively.
“Most of the time, she’s not in uniform; she just blends in,” Lively said. “There are people you don’t see working, but they do plenty for this community.”
Taylor said she was drawn to Rome and Floyd County because of what she’d heard about the agencies.
“I wasn’t from the area, but I was encouraged by people that were employed here to apply because there were good opportunities for women in law enforcement,” Taylor said. “So that’s how I started, and 15 years later, I’m still here.”
At the end of the awards, the families of many of the law enforcement officers were brought up, thanked and given flowers in appreciation for supporting their spouses who work hard to keep the community safe.
